# K5.6 Cross-entropy gradient written in place in BF16

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Class: **Bitwise** when every per-token `grad_output` is 0 or a power of two;
**Same function** (one extra BF16 rounding) otherwise (Section 4)

## 1. Packages

G3, G6 and G6b, where named below, are Firmus's earlier GPT-OSS NVFP4 packages (`nemo_g3_nvfp4_v1`, `nemo_g6_nvfp4_v2`,
`nemo_g6b_nvfp4_v2_1`), withdrawn from this submission and no longer in this repository. Their values, line numbers,
images and test jobs are cited as the record of where evidence was collected ([Index](../KERNELS.md), "Earlier packages").

- `NVFP4_CE_BF16_INPLACE=1` (config line 89).
  Same value in G3, G6 and G6b and G6c. Cross-entropy fusion runs TE's Triton implementation (`CE_FUSION_IMPL="te"`,
  config L14; `cross_entropy_loss_fusion` default True, `conf/gpt_oss.yaml` L94).
- Code: TE `transformer_engine/pytorch/triton/cross_entropy.py`, modified by
  `docker/patches/transformer_engine_firmus_nvfp4.patch` L3477–3530 (byte-identical in the three packages). No
  `pretrain.py` hook.

## 2. What the reference does

TE `27486e03` `cross_entropy_forward` computes, in one Triton pass over the logits, the per-token loss and the
gradient \(\mathrm{softmax}(x) - \mathrm{onehot}(y)\) in FP32, and stores the gradient in a new FP32 buffer
(patch context L3501–3502). `cross_entropy_backward` multiplies that buffer by the per-token `grad_output`
(skipped when `grad_output` equals the scalar 1.0, L3517–3529) and autograd casts the FP32 result to the BF16
logits' dtype. One rounding to BF16: \(\mathrm{bf16}(g_{32}\cdot c)\).

## 3. What this implementation does

1. `_INPLACE_GRAD` is read once at import (L3493).
2. With it set, `grad_input = _input` (L3503–3510): the forward kernel writes each row block's gradient into the
   logits tensor after reading that block; the loss uses the target logit read before the overwrite (comment
   L3504–3506). The gradient is stored as BF16: \(\mathrm{bf16}(g_{32})\).
3. The backward's skip test now builds the scalar 1.0 only when `grad_output` has one element (L3523–3527), which
   avoids a stream synchronisation for a per-token `grad_output`; a per-token `grad_output` is multiplied in as
   before.

## 4. Why the result is the same, and when it is not

Loss: unchanged, 0 differing elements in every test case. Gradient stored by the forward:
\(\mathrm{bf16}(g_{32})\), the same value the reference produces after its cast. With `grad_output` = 1 the result
is bitwise. With a per-token `grad_output` \(c\) the in-place result is \(\mathrm{bf16}(\mathrm{bf16}(g_{32})\cdot c)\),
two roundings instead of one; it equals the reference when \(c\) is 0 or a power of two (no subnormals), and can
differ by one BF16 step otherwise.

vs reference / vs FP64 (test `k5_5_k5_6_glu_ce`, job 22220, G6 image; real shape 8192 × 3 × 201 088):
- `grad_output` = 1: dlogits 0 differ.
- random per-token `grad_output`: 1 286 686 635 of 4 941 938 688 differ, max difference 2^-8;
  captured logits of a G6 run with seeded labels, job 22497: 820 886 080 (iteration 4) and 820 448 946
  (iteration 303) differ.
- constant 1/N with 10 % of tokens masked (Megatron's form when the loss is averaged over tokens): 1 167 977 504
  differ, max difference 2.4e-7.
- vs FP64 (1024 × 3 tokens), FP32 buffer / in place: 1/N 0.0019581 / 0.0019587 rel L2; random 0.0014903 /
  0.0014905.

Which case training is in depends on Megatron's per-token `grad_output` (Section 9).

## 5. Numerics

Forward arithmetic unchanged (FP32 in the kernel). Storage of the gradient BF16 instead of FP32; the backward
multiply then reads and writes BF16. The logits tensor is overwritten by design.

## 6. Shapes and fallbacks

- **Gate:** none besides the switch. `_INPLACE_GRAD` (L3493) applies to every call of `cross_entropy_forward`,
  whatever the logits dtype.
- **Falls back:** never. FP32 logits get an FP32 gradient written over them (0 differ vs the reference); FP16
  logits get an FP16 gradient (75 978 695 elements differ vs the FP32-buffer reference, test case
  `fallback_fp16_logits`).
- **Assumes:** (a) the logits are not read after the cross-entropy forward, by the caller or by another autograd
  node: the code does not check it, and a later reader would see the gradient. In this model the logits come from
  the output layer and only the loss is used (the output layer's backward needs its input and weight, not the
  logits). (b) In evaluation the forward also overwrites the logits; only the loss is used there.
- **Check:** config line 89. No log line; the switch is read at import, so the
  config value is the value used.

## 7. Code

- `transformer_engine_firmus_nvfp4.patch` L3477–3530: `_INPLACE_GRAD` L3493, in-place buffer L3503–3510, skip
  test L3517–3529. Applied by `Dockerfile` step 4
  (`git apply` L113).

## 8. Tests and evidence

Kernel test on the submitted image (Firmus test script `k5_5_k5_6_glu_ce.py`, available on request),
`_INPLACE_GRAD` True vs False, and vs FP64 for small shapes. The case counts below cover the edge, fallback and
fixture cases only; the main comparisons are separate rows in the test records and give the figures in Section 4.

- Job 22886 (this package's image; logits from the output-layer input and weight captured in its training run, job 22873), 53 cases with K5.5 (also run as jobs 22927 / 22928, `../KERNELS.md` section 9). K5.6 cases with
  a difference: `fallback_fp16_logits` (Section 6; there is no dtype gate, so this is the FP16 in-place result,
  not a fallback) and `fixture_label_smoothing_1e-3` (by design). Run a vs run b: every digest equal; repeats one
  digest; prefill and fresh process 0 differ; inputs passed as copies unchanged.
- Earlier runs on the G6 image, jobs 22220 and 22497: the figures in Section 4.

## 9. Open points

1. The per-token `grad_output` in training is not established from the package: Megatron-Bridge and Megatron-LM
   compute it (`calculate_per_token_loss`, division by the token count) outside the package. If it is the loss
   mask divided by the number of tokens (not a power of two), K5.6 is **Same function**, not Bitwise. This package sets
   `eod_mask_loss=True` (`pretrain.py` L1014), so the masked tokens' `grad_output` is 0.
2. Section 4 quotes the main-comparison figures of jobs 22220 and 22497 only; those of jobs 22415 and 22636 are
   in the test records (available on request) and are not quoted here.
3. TE's backward multiply (`element_mul_kernel`) is upstream code, not in the patch; the two-rounding description
   rests on the patch context and the measured differences.
